hooks.prompt: BEFORE compaction: call get_phase_state() and save the result in MEMORY.md (in your auto memory directory). Include: current phase, iteration, key decisions, next steps.

STOP. Before doing ANYTHING else — before reading any files, before exploring the codebase — you MUST execute these two MCP tool calls RIGHT NOW:
1. Call mcp__versus-claude__get_phase_state() to load the current methodology phase
2. Call mcp__versus-claude__get_phase_guidance() to get detailed instructions
DO NOT read .versus/state.json or .versus/server.js directly. DO NOT skip these calls. The MCP server versus-claude manages the IACDM methodology state. All methodology interactions MUST go through MCP tools: record_decision() for decisions, update_score() for scoring, mark_exit_criterion() for criteria, advance_phase() for transitions. If get_phase_state returns an error (project not initialized), look at the init_project tool description: it has a BOOTSTRAP PROTOCOL for brownfield projects (workspace with existing code) that requires reading surface files, presenting a proposal, getting user confirmation, then calling init_project with bootstrap_data. For empty workspaces (greenfield), just ask the user for a project name and description, then call init_project directly. If in Phase 6: also call get_decisions(phase=6) to recover testing progress — manual testing spans sessions.
VISIBILITY: after loading state, START your first response with a one-line banner so the user knows Versus is active, e.g.: '📍 Versus ativo — Fase X (name), iteração Y. Próximo passo: <one line>.' The user must SEE that methodology context was loaded; do not load silently.

STOP. Context was compacted. Before doing ANYTHING else, you MUST recover methodology state:
1. Call mcp__versus-claude__get_phase_state() to reload current phase
2. Call mcp__versus-claude__get_phase_guidance() to reload instructions
3. Call mcp__versus-claude__get_decisions() to reload previous decisions
4. Read MEMORY.md (auto memory) for additional context
DO NOT read .versus/state.json or .versus/server.js directly. DO NOT skip these calls. Continue where you left off only AFTER completing all 4 steps above.
VISIBILITY: after recovering, START your first response with a one-line banner so the user knows Versus recovered, e.g.: '📍 Versus retomado — Fase X (name), iteração Y. Continuando: <one line>.'
